title: Emrys and the House
premise: Juniper Voss takes a teaching post at Hollowmere Academy, where students vanish mid-semester and the founders' ledgers suggest the school itself is fed, not run. His nightly sleep recordings begin capturing a second voice — patient, ancient, answering his questions in his own timbre — and he realizes the house has chosen him as its next vessel. To save a missing student he loves, Juniper must complete the founders' interrupted ritual: not to bind the house, but to unmake it, trading his own name and memory as the price. In the end the school stands empty and ordinary, and a man with no past signs the guestbook as its new caretaker.
about_author: Isandro Sterling is the pen name of a former night-shift archivist who spent six years cataloguing the papers of defunct boarding schools. They write horror about institutions that remember more than the people inside them.

chapters.title: Enrollment
chapters.summary: Juniper arrives at Hollowmere Academy on a fog-bound October evening, signing a guestbook whose earlier entries are all in identical handwriting. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: hopeful unease — he wants belonging badly enough to ignore the wrongness of the welcome.

chapters.title: The Missing-Class Problem
chapters.summary: Teaching his first weeks, Juniper notices attendance rosters that shrink overnight and students who insist a classmate 'was never here.' The headmistress, Wren Halloway, deflects with practiced warmth. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: creeping gaslight; documentation becomes his anchor against doubt.

chapters.title: Documentation Is a Kind of Prayer
chapters.summary: Juniper begins recording himself sleeping to catch what he suspects he's forgetting by day. The tapes capture a second voice — calm, familiar — answering questions he doesn't remember asking. POV: Juniper, interleaved with tape transcripts. Emotional beat: dread of self-betrayal; the horror is inside his own mouth.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Juniper confronts Wren, who admits she was a missing student returned 'wrong,' kept alive by the house as long as she serves it. She warns him to leave before winter solstice. POV: Wren for the first time. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness between two people owned by the same thing.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: In the archive, Juniper finds the founders' ritual half-finished in 1911: a rite to feed the house a vessel and gain immortality for the school. One founder's page ends mid-sentence. POV: Juniper with ledger excerpts. Emotional beat: terrible understanding — the pattern has been repeating for a century.

chapters.title: The Second Voice
chapters.summary: The voice in the recordings starts speaking while Juniper is awake, wearing his memories like borrowed clothes. It offers him permanence: stay, be loved by the house, never be lonely again. POV: split Juniper/voice. Emotional beat: seduction — belonging offered at the price of identity.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: A student Juniper loves, Ada, is taken into the walls on solstice eve; the house demands its vessel now. Wren reveals the ritual can be reversed — completed backward — but only from inside, and only by someone the house trusts. POV: alternating Juniper and Wren. Emotional beat: love against duty; he chooses Ada over survival.

chapters.title: Inside the House
chapters.summary: Juniper lets the voice take him under, waking in the house's interior — corridors of recorded voices, every missing student preserved as sound. He finds Ada and begins the reversed rite, unbinding names from the walls. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: grief and resolve amid the beautiful, awful chorus of the kept.

chapters.title: The Unmaking
chapters.summary: The voice fights him with his own longing, offering a life where he was always home. Juniper speaks his own name into the rite and gives it up; the house convulses, releasing the students as the recordings burn to silence. POV: Juniper dissolving into third person. Emotional beat: climax — identity surrendered freely, which is the one price the house cannot digest.

chapters.title: Guestbook
chapters.summary: Spring: Hollowmere stands empty, sold, ordinary. A caretaker with no memory of his name tends the grounds; Ada visits, leaves flowers, and cannot say why she weeps. He signs the guestbook in fresh handwriting. POV: Ada, closing on the caretaker. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution — belonging achieved by becoming no one, love persisting without memory.
